mainProgression.description: High-tempo garage rock shuffle riff in A, moving into sharp staccato power chords and a driving ♭VII - IV - I chorus.

sectionProgressions.progression: Single-note A walkup into A5 - C5 - D5
sectionProgressions.description: Fast-driving single note walkup answering the tambourine before stabbing into power chords
Muted percussive eighth-note rhythm with sudden dynamic stops
The classic rock double-plagal turnaround driving the anthemic vocal hook

harmonicFunction: A5 (I5) - The stomping garage rock home tonic
C5 (♭III5) - Blues-rock minor third power chord creating gritty push
D5 (IV5) - Subdominant chord completing the energetic riff cadence
G (♭VII) - Mixolydian subtonic chord that gives the chorus its triumphant pub rock drive

techniques.name: High-Tempo Motown Shuffle & Staccato Power Stabs
techniques.description: Strumming tight, palm-muted power chords at a blistering 205 BPM tempo, cutting off note decay instantly with fretting-hand mutes

notes: Intro walkup: Open low E → fret 3 (G) → fret 4 (G#) → open A string
Power chords: A5 (fret 5 low E), C5 (fret 3 A), D5 (fret 5 A)
sequence: Lock into the tambourine and hi-hat beat on beats 2 and 4
Execute the chromatic walkup on the low strings
Stab the power chords cleanly with downstrokes
Choke all strings immediately on beat 4 for dramatic silence
tips: Keep your right-hand wrist loose: tense forearms will fatigue quickly at 205 BPM
Cameron Muncey used a Gibson Flying V through a cranked Marshall JCM800 for maximum Australian pub crunch
Honor every stop: the tight full-band rests make the song sound huge

sections.name: High-Octane Intro Riff
sections.description: One of the definitive guitar hooks of the 2000s garage rock revival.
notes: Fast chromatic bass walkup on low E
Staccato power chord stabs on A5, C5, and D5
Maintain relentless forward energy at 205 BPM

sections.name: Chorus Anthem
sections.description: The soaring chorus 'So what you got to say? She's with me and I'm with her'.
notes: Accent the transition from G to D to A
Let the final A chord ring with stadium power

sections.name: Blues Guitar Solo
sections.description: Cameron Muncey's raw, Chuck Berry-inspired blues solo in the 5th position.
notes: Aggressive pick attack with natural tube saturation
Quick double-stops on the high E and B strings

guitar.recommended: Gibson Flying V or Gibson ES-335
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for biting garage-rock cut and high-mid punch

effects.distortion: Ibanez TS9 Tube Screamer (for solo boost)
effects.other: Heavy celluloid plectrums (1.0mm) for fast downstrokes

beginner.title: Chorus Chords & Rhythm
steps: Learn the open G, D, and A chords
Practice shifting between them at a comfortable 140 BPM
Build speed up to the album tempo of 205 BPM

intermediate.title: Main Riff & Staccato Mutes
steps: Learn the chromatic intro walkup on the low strings
Master the A5, C5, and D5 power chord stabs with clean hand mutes
Lock tightly with the fast drum beat without dragging or rushing

advanced.title: Solo & Full-Speed Endurance
steps: Learn Cameron Muncey's fast 5th-position blues solo note-for-note
Build right-hand stamina to play all 3.5 minutes at 205 BPM with zero tension
Perform live with authentic Australian pub rock swagger

commonMistakes: Tensing up the right forearm during the 205 BPM shuffle rhythm
Letting open strings ring during the silent stop-time pauses
Rushing ahead of the drum beat on the intro walkup
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Chromatic walkup at 150 BPM → 180 BPM → 205 BPM
5 minutes: Power chord staccato muting drill with metronome
focusAreas: Right-hand wrist relaxation at high tempo
Crisp silence on the stop-time chokes
metronomeWork: Start metronome at 160 BPM to ensure clean pick placement
Advance by 10 BPM increments to 205 BPM
